Interactive Demo

How Your Cat Actually Sees Colors

Cats are dichromats—they see blues and yellows vividly, while reds look muted brown/gray.

1

The 5-Step Hunting Cycle

Cats are wired for Stalk → Chase → Pounce → Catch → Eat. Digital games nail the first three steps, so tossing a real kicker toy or 2 treats right after exiting prevents frustration.

Stalk Chase Pounce Real Toy Finish
2

Why 3–5 Minute Bursts Work Best

In the wild, feline hunts are short sprints, not marathons. Our built-in 3-minute and 5-minute timers keep play exciting without causing overstimulation or screen obsession.

Best routine: 3 min Play Arena → 2 min physical wand toy → 1 small treat.
3

Reading Play Body Language

Happy focus: Forward ears, dilated pupils, butt wiggle, gentle tail-tip twitch.
Time for a break: Flattened "airplane" ears, fast tail thumping, or biting the tablet edge.

4

Protecting Your Tablet Screen

Most cats tap with soft paw pads, but excited pounces can bring out claws. Trim claw tips gently, place the tablet on a non-slip rug, or add a matte tempered glass protector.
